title: 美国选举花费逼近饱和点 资金流向与候选人效应成焦点
speaker: Bloomberg

segments.en: We start with the business of elections in the U.S., with just over a week until the nation votes on control of Congress and the governorships of 33 states, enormous amounts of money
segments.zh: 我们从美国选举的商业运作说起，距离决定国会控制权和33个州长职位的投票仅剩一周多，大量资金正涌入竞选活动、政党和政治行动委员会。

segments.en: are pouring into campaigns, parties, and packs. Where is it all coming from? And what difference is it likely to make? Blair Efron of Centerview Partners has been involved in Democratic fundraising
segments.zh: 这些钱从何而来？又可能带来什么影响？Centerview Partners的布莱尔·埃夫隆多年来参与民主党筹款，他表示至少有一点是确定的：选举成本只会越来越高。

segments.en: for years, and he says at least one thing is certain. Elections aren't getting any cheaper.
segments.zh: 这些竞选的成本呈指数级增长。一场参议院竞选将花费超过2亿美元，而国会竞选过去只需500万到1000万美元。

segments.en: The cost of these races has gone up exponentially. A Senate race is going to be $200 million plus. A congressional race which used to be $5 million, $10 million to spend, and what I would
segments.zh: 信不信由你，大部分资金仍来自小额捐赠者，直接流向候选人。而商界则大量通过政治行动委员会捐款。

segments.en: say is that, believe it or not, the most money still comes from small-dollar donors. That goes direct to the candidates. What you see a lot from the business community is going to packs.
segments.zh: 我认为大多数关注政策和华盛顿事务的人都在想办法对两党都提供帮助。

segments.en: I think most people who have an interest in things policy and things DC are figuring out how
segments.zh: 钱重要吗？从这个意义上说，我们看到一些竞选，比如密歇根州的初选，我家乡密歇根州，埃尔赛义德对阵史蒂文斯，资金差距很大，但并未转化为选票。

segments.en: to be helpful to both sides. Does the money matter? I mean, in this sense, we've seen some races, for example, the primary in Michigan. My home state in Michigan, Elsaid against Stevens,
segments.zh: 对双方都有帮助。资金重要吗？我的意思是，从这个意义上说，我们已经看到一些竞选，例如密歇根州的初选。我的家乡密歇根州，埃尔赛义德对阵史蒂文斯，

segments.en: and there was a big difference in the money, but it didn't translate into the votes.
segments.zh: 资金差距很大，但并未转化为选票。
